docs.title: Q1: Who is Silitex S.r.l.?
docs.text: An Italian specialty-chemicals producer in Cologna Veneta (Verona) describing itself as 'alta tecnologia dell'emulsione' — high emulsion technology. The group includes Silitex, Unispray and Silitex Chemicals and sells in more than 30 countries through selected distributors, with regional technical support. (source: silitex.it/en/company)

docs.text: Viale Industria 34, 37044 Cologna Veneta (VR), Italy — tel. +39 0442 411561. The site is published in Italian, English, French and German. (source: silitex.it/en/company)

docs.title: Q3: What product families does Silitex make?
docs.text: 35 published categories: silicone and silicone-free antifoams (food-grade, high-temperature, polyether, vegetal, powdered, solvent), wetting/levelling additives, cationic and silicone softeners, emulsions/micro/nano-emulsions, leather finishes, mould-release and welding detaching agents, antistatics for offset, wax emulsions, sewing-yarn lubricants, water/stain repellents, silicone rubbers, pastes and greases, linear fluids, resins, polyelectrolytes, de-emulsifiers, detergents and aerosols. (source: silitex.it/en/products/range-of-products)

docs.title: Q4: Which management-system certifications does Silitex hold?
docs.text: The master catalog lists ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2023, plus a HACCP-certified facility for the food-grade line (January 2025) and GOTS-ICEA approval for organic textile auxiliaries. (source: Master catalog v2 — Executive Summary)

docs.title: Q5: Does Silitex work with distributors or sell direct?
docs.text: Silitex states it is present in 30+ countries 'through selected, highly qualified distributors', supported by regional technical teams — the model this Israel proposal fits into. (source: silitex.it/en/company)

docs.title: Q6: What is the difference between an antifoam and a defoamer?
docs.text: Both are the same chemistry used differently: an antifoam is dosed before foam forms (prevention), a defoamer is added to collapse existing foam (knock-down). Silitex emulsions such as BERETEX, DYNAPAN and ANTISCHIUMA 3 do both; the product sheet usually states 'immediate knock-down and lasting effect'. (source: products dataset)

docs.title: Q7: Which Silitex antifoam replaces Dow Corning Antifoam A / DC 1520 / XIAMETER AFE-1520?
docs.text: ANTISCHIUMA 3 (10–30% active, FDA/BfR/EPA, food contact) and the BERETEX 350/500/750 series (35/50/75% active PDMS emulsions) are the direct cross-reference in the master catalog. (source: offsets v5, CAT-04)

docs.title: Q8: What does the number in BERETEX 350 / 500 / 750 mean?
docs.text: Active silicone content in the emulsion: 35%, 50% and 75%. Higher active = lower dosage and smaller drums, but needs more dilution control; 350 is 'ready to use or pre-dilutable', 750 is the concentrate for low-dosage automated systems. (source: products dataset)

docs.title: Q9: Which antifoam survives pH 14 caustic cleaning?
docs.text: DYNAKOS 130 E — a caustic-stable silicone emulsion rated pH 1–14, positioned for extreme alkaline cleaners, pulp bleaching and CIP caustic systems. (source: products dataset SIL-ANT-017)

docs.title: Q10: What is a polyether-silicone antifoam and when do I need it?
docs.text: A silicone modified with PEG/PPG chains (DYNAWEED MS 4, 200 E, 260 E) that stays dispersible across pH 1–13 and survives thermal shock up to ~130 °C — the choice for high-temperature jet dyeing, bleaching baths and alkaline CIP where plain PDMS emulsions break. (source: products dataset)

docs.title: Q11: Do you have a 100% active antifoam compound for slurries?
docs.text: STHOR 1000 — anhydrous dimethicone/silica compound, 2000–5000 cSt, for mineral slurries, wastewater sludge, mining and drilling where a water emulsion would be diluted away. (source: products dataset SIL-ANT-018)

docs.title: Q12: Which antifoam is best for automated dosing pumps?
docs.text: BERETEX 1000 AD — low viscosity (100–300 cSt) emulsion designed for pumpability in automated dosing of liquid detergents and chemical washing lines. (source: products dataset SIL-ANT-006)

docs.title: Q13: What replaces Momentive SAG 30 or Wacker SILFOAM SE 2?
docs.text: SAG 30 → BERETEX 350 / DYNAPAN 30 D; SILFOAM SE 2 → ANTISCHIUMA 3. The Offset Sniper page resolves any competitor code to the Silitex equivalent. (source: offsets v5)

docs.title: Q14: What does 'E900' mean on SILIFOOD products?
docs.text: E900 is the EU food-additive number for dimethylpolysiloxane (simethicone). SILIFOOD 1600 and 3000 K are E900 water emulsions approved for direct food contact under FDA 21 CFR 173.340 and EU rules. (source: food-grade line)

docs.title: Q15: Which Silitex products are Kosher certified?
docs.text: SILIFOOD 30, SILIFOOD 1600, SILIFOOD 2500, SILIFOOD 3000 K, CPL 350 and CPL 350 ET carry Kosher certificates (SILIFOOD line also Halal). ANTISCHIUMA 3 and CPL 2907 are food-contact compliant. (source: Master catalog — Kosher & FDA sheet)

docs.title: Q16: What is the recommended dosage of SILIFOOD in food processing?
docs.text: Typically 10–50 ppm: SILIFOOD 30 10–50 ppm, SILIFOOD 1600 10–30 ppm, SILIFOOD 2500 10–40 ppm, SILIFOOD 3000 K 10–50 ppm. CPL 350 / 350 ET 2–30 ppm. Always confirm with the TDS and local food law. (source: Master catalog — Kosher & FDA sheet)

docs.text: CPL 350 / CPL 350 ET — anhydrous, 100% active, fully vegetal fatty-acid compounds; 350 ET is self-emulsifying in cold water and formulated for bio-fermentation and commercial yeast. Both Kosher certified, FDA direct food additive. (source: food-grade line)

docs.title: Q18: What is the added value of a Silitex antifoam in the food industry?
docs.text: Four things: regulatory cover (E900, FDA 21 CFR, Kosher/Halal, HACCP plant), process yield (less foam = fuller tanks, faster bottling, fewer overflows), very low dosage (10–50 ppm) and thermal/pH stability (ANTISCHIUMA 3 survives thermal treatment). For Israel the Kosher certificate is a hard requirement most global brands cannot show on the drum. (source: food-grade line + products dataset)

docs.title: Q19: Which antifoam for sugar refining and fruit washing?

docs.title: Q20: Which antifoam is FDA-approved for food-contact paper and packaging?
docs.text: CPL 2907 — 100% active self-emulsifying fatty-alcohol compound, silicone-free, FDA 21 CFR approved for paper & cardboard in direct food contact; dosage 0.1–0.5 kg/ton pulp. (source: Master catalog)

docs.title: Q21: What is FISIOREX 1000?
docs.text: Silitex's 100% plant-based, highly biodegradable antifoam/adjuvant with zero synthetic silicone — for eco-label detergents, green paints, organic agrochemicals and waterborne coatings. It replaces synthetic non-ionic surfactants and products like SEPPIC Green or Lexfeel N. (source: products dataset BIO-ANT-001)

docs.title: Q22: Does Silitex have D4 in its products, and how does it replace cyclic siloxanes?
docs.text: Under EU REACH (Annex XVII, entries 70 and extensions) the cyclic siloxanes D4, D5 and D6 are restricted in wash-off and, progressively, leave-on and industrial uses; D4 is classified PBT/vPvB and reprotoxic. Silitex addresses this in three ways: (1) dedicated non-cyclic amino emulsions manufactured without cyclic siloxanes — MACROAMISIL (E1386), MICROAMISIL (E1352) and the hydrophilic IDROAMISIL 250 (E1453) — drop-in replacements for soft hand, swelling and durable water repellency; (2) linear PDMS as carrier instead of volatile cyclics — the Silitex DIMETHICONE cosmetic fluids (5 to 5,000 cSt) and FLUIDO DI SILICONE line, the EVERSIL emulsions, and elastomer gels on a 'Dimethicone (and) Dimethicone Crosspolymer' base; (3) silicone-free, 100% bio-based alternatives — FISIOREX 1000, EVEROIL 35 / EVERIX 35. Products that still carry a cyclic carrier (e.g. CICLOPENTASILOSSANO (D5) / Volatile D5 fluid for cosmetics) are clearly identified. Confirm the cyclic content on each SDS section 3 before specifying. Talk track if challenged on CICLOPENTASILOSSANO (D5) / D5: (1) acknowledge the legacy SKU — it stays in the catalog for non-EU markets and industrial uses where a volatile D5 carrier is still permitted; (2) for REACH-sensitive cosmetic/personal-care accounts always check SDS §3 for exact cyclic content (D4 impurity limit < 0.1%); (3) pivot to the seamless upgrade — linear Silitex DM dimethicones / dimethicone-crosspolymer gels, or 100% vegetal EVEROIL 35 / EVERIX 35. Chemists respect a distributor who knows the regulatory reality better than the marketing claim. (source: silitex.it softeners page + products dataset + REACH Annex XVII)

docs.title: Q23: Which products are GOTS-ICEA approved for organic textiles?
docs.text: The GOTS-ICEA certified textile auxiliary line including MACROAMISIL (E1386) and MICROAMISIL (41/C/E1352); the master catalog lists the whole group under CAT-19. (source: offsets v5 CAT-19)

docs.title: Q24: What is Silitex's approach to the non-silicone trend in personal care and cosmetics?
docs.text: Three tracks. (1) 100% plant-based emollients — EVEROIL 35 / EVERIX 35 (vegetal emollient and softener emulsions for eco-label toiletries and natural skin/hair care) plus natural wax emulsions CARNAUBEX (carnauba) and WASPER D (beeswax) to replace silicone films. (2) Dedicated silicone-free lines — FISIOREX 1000 (100% vegetable fatty-acid active, zero synthetic silicone oil or solvent) and whole catalog categories of non-silicone fluids and silicone-free antifoams/de-aerators. (3) Where silicone performance is still required: D4/D5-free non-cyclic emulsions (MACROAMISIL E1386, MICROAMISIL E1352, IDROAMISIL 250 E1453) and linear dimethicone carriers instead of cyclics. Comparison for R&D — EVEROIL/EVERIX vs. EVERSIL/BODYSIL: origin 100% vegetal vs. linear PDMS; cyclics none vs. non-cyclic PDMS but subject to REACH purity limits; certifications EU Eco-Label / natural-cosmetic compliant vs. standard; feel natural non-greasy velvet softness vs. intense slip, high gloss, hydrophobic film; biodegradability high (fatty-acid structure) vs. inert slow-degrading polymer. Dual-track selling: lead with EVEROIL/EVERIX for clean-beauty, Eco-Label or vegan claims; recommend EVERSIL 35 / BODYSIL when the customer needs maximum shine, slip and water repellency. (source: silitex.it range of products + products dataset)

docs.title: Q25: What is the difference between a macro-, micro- and nano-emulsion softener?

Microemulsions (MICROAMISIL, STONIX — translucent) penetrate yarns for wash-fast softness. Nanoemulsions (NANOAMISIL HR, <30 nm, water-clear) penetrate deepest — for microfibre, technical yarns and premium hand feel. (source: products dataset + silitex.it)

docs.title: Q38: Which lubricant is used for sewing thread?

docs.text: CARNAUBEX (C / 442) carnauba wax, WASPER D beeswax, POLYEMUL (TS / 800/38) paraffin and the IDROCER family of polyethylene-wax nano-emulsions (SH = high melting point, transparent film). (source: silitex.it water-repellents page + products dataset)

docs.title: Q41: What silicone raw materials does Silitex supply?
docs.text: Per the 2026 sector catalogues (received 13/10/2026): cosmetic raw materials — DIMETHICONE 1.5 cSt to 5000 cSt, DISILOXANE, CYCLOPENTASILOXANE (D4 <0.1%), DIMETHICONOL GUM, PHENYL TRIMETHICONE, AMODIMETHICONE, PEG-10 / PEG-12 DIMETHICONE, DIMETISIL 18/18 P (PEG/PPG-18/18), DIVICROSS (crosspolymer), IDROSIL (trimethylsiloxysilicate), SINTOSIL (polymethylsilsesquioxane), C13-15 / C15-19 ALKANE, ISODODECANE, TETRADECANE, DODECANE; blends BODY BLEND, CICLODIMETIBLEND, DIMETIBLEND, SILIBLEND DT 50, SILIBLEND CROSS D, DIMEPOL 18/18, ESABLEND, ALKABLEND 6800; emulsions BODYSIL 60, BODYAMISIL 20/35/50/LF, BODYAMODIMETISIL 60, MICROAMODIMETISIL 200. Industrial: FLUIDO DI SILICONE 5–2,000,000 cSt, SILICONE FLUID food & pharma grades, H 160 / H 180, AMINOQUAT 1000, IDROAMISIL 1000. Only cetyl dimethicone and caprylyl methicone remain absent. (source: offsets v5 CAT-11/12/20/31/36/37)

docs.title: Q42: Why is the D4/D5-free portfolio a commercial argument in Israel?
docs.text: Israeli paint, detergent, textile and cosmetics manufacturers follow EU REACH and ECHA guidance closely because they export to the EU. Many legacy competitor softeners and emulsions still ride on cyclic-siloxane (D4/D5) carriers. Offering a certified non-cyclic alternative (MACROAMISIL E1386, MICROAMISIL E1352, IDROAMISIL 250 E1453) plus linear-PDMS and bio-based options lets the distributor open the conversation on compliance, not price — and a REACH survey of the customer's current products is the natural first technical service. (source: products dataset; REACH Annex XVII)

docs.title: Q43: Which documents accompany a Silitex product?
docs.text: Technical Data Sheet (TDS), Safety Data Sheet (SDS/MSDS, EU CLP format), certificates where applicable (Kosher, Halal, FDA/BfR statements, GOTS-ICEA) and ISO 9001/14001/45001 company certificates. In this CRM they are stored in the Knowledge Base and searchable from 'Ask Silitex'. (source: Master catalog)

docs.title: Q44: What is BfR XXXVI and which products comply?
docs.text: German BfR Recommendation XXXVI covers paper and board for food contact. VOLUMEX / VOLUSOFT (paper softeners) and IDROCER PE-wax emulsions are listed as BfR / FDA packaging compliant. (source: products dataset)
